equity_bridge.item: Investments and other financial assets at book (innovation fund, post Epiminder write-down)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR capital employed table, 30 June 2026 (189.4 a year earlier). Their income/losses are outside the flows; new innovation-fund outlays (13.8 in FY26) are likewise not charged in capex.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment between revenue_3yr_cagr (6.6) and the FY27 guide; equity CAGR rejected
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~0%) diverges far more than 30% from revenue CAGR (6.6% / 9.4%). Book value is flat because Cochlear pays out ~70% of underlying profit and wrote off 109.1 of innovation-fund investments (Epiminder) in FY26; it is not a growth signal. Statutory EPS CAGRs are distorted by FY26 significant items (cloud expense 66.0 and investment write-downs 109.1 after tax): underlying basic EPS went 464.1c (FY23) -> 392.0c (FY26 on the LTI basis), about -5.5% a year.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner series (CSV FCF - share-based payment expense - interest income): FY21 188.1, FY23 234.1, FY26 255.0. Reported FCF CAGRs are 1.3% (3yr) and 6.9% (5yr), so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow. Lease principal is not deducted in the historical series (not collected for older years), and FY26 includes a 58.6 working-capital release, so the 3-year figure flatters the underlying trend.

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 lands at the guidance midpoint (low single-digit constant-currency growth, underlying NPAT ~340). Developed-market cochlear implant growth, flat in FY26 on US insurance-claim delays, UK surgery backlogs and share loss in Germany and the UK, recovers gradually as the Nucleus Nexa system (>95% of developed-market implant sales by June 2026, ~3% price rise) and the ENT referral pilots take hold; services keep growing with the installed recipient base; China stays a volume-not-value market under volume-based procurement. Revenue growth returns to 6.5-7% -- below the 9.4% five-year CAGR -- and fades to 4.5%. Underlying EBIT margin rebuilds from ~19% to ~22% (FY24 level) as FY26's transitional costs and under-recovered factory overhead drop out, but R&D stays near 14% of sales for the drug-eluting electrode and totally implantable implant, so the 18% net margin target is not reached.
scenario_narratives.bull: The developed-market adult segment re-accelerates: referral-pathway work and direct-to-consumer surgeries (up 10% in the US in FY26) lift market growth, Nexa's upgradeable firmware and the drug-eluting electrode sustain price and share, Osia keeps expanding Acoustics outside the US, and upgrade cycles drive services. Revenue compounds ~9% through FY31 (the pre-FY26 run rate), gross margin recovers to ~74% as volumes refill the factories, and operating leverage takes underlying EBIT margin to ~24%, i.e. the 18% net margin target, with the cloud programme finishing in FY27.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY26 was not a pothole. Developed-market penetration of adult candidates stays stuck, payer friction in the US and public-system capacity in Western Europe cap procedure growth, competitors (Advanced Bionics/Sonova, MED-EL) hold the share they took in Germany and the UK, and China VBP pricing spreads to more provinces and to sound-processor upgrades. Growth settles at ~3% nominal, mix keeps shifting to lower-priced emerging-market units, and margins stay at FY26 levels because R&D and the cloud programme cannot be cut without damaging the franchise.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cochlear is a debt-free global leader in implantable hearing with a large annuity-like services base, valued on strict owner cash flow: lease payments, the cash cost of settling share awards, and a tail of cloud-programme spend are all charged, interest on the cash pile is stripped, and working capital (34% of sales) is charged on growth. The valuation rests on how far and how fast the underlying EBIT margin rebuilds from FY26's ~18.5% toward the 22-24% it earned in FY24-FY25, and on whether developed-market implant growth returns.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin recovery: each 1pp of mature EBITDA margin moves base value by roughly 4-5%; the base assumes ~22% underlying EBIT, the bear ~18.5%.

Cloud computing expense (94.3 pre-tax in FY26, 32.7 in FY25) is treated by the company as a one-off significant item; if it recurs beyond the 2.0% of sales assumed over FY27-28 the base is overstated.
Developed-market volume: US payer delays, UK/Spain capacity constraints and share loss in Germany and the UK drove flat implant revenue in FY26.
China volume-based procurement and emerging-market mix lower average selling prices and gross margin.
Currency: ~90%+ of sales are outside Australia; the AUD flows embed FY26 exchange rates and hedge outcomes.
Terminal value is the majority of enterprise value; Gordon growth of 3% at a 9% WACC implies a ~17x exit multiple on owner FCF.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 88.74-284.88
data_sources.financials: COH.AX_Metrics.csv and core_metrics/kpis (H1 FY2015-FY2026); Cochlear Annual Report FY2026 (review of operations p21-25, five-year performance history, cash-flow statement, EPS note, lease note 6.4, outlook statement)
data_sources.qualitative: COH.AX_Analysis.json (bull/bear cases, risks, guidance) and the FY2026 annual report review of operations and outlook

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares FY2026 (65,535,591; FY26 AR EPS note: basic 65,417,231 + 118,360 dilutive options/rights). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows at the cash cost of buying shares on-market to satisfy awards, so diluting as well would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR. P&L share-based payment expense was 12.1 (depressed by LTI reversals after the FY26 miss; FY25 22.1). The owner-cost figure used is the cash 'Outlay from exercise of share options and performance rights' of 26.6 (FY25 24.3) from the FY26 cash-flow review -- the cash Cochlear spends buying shares on-market to settle awards, which is what keeps the count flat. It REPLACES the 12.1 expense; the two are not summed. Cochlear does not disclose tax withheld on awards separately.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: ~4.4% Australian 10-year government bond + ~0.85 beta x ~5.5% ERP = ~9.0% cost of equity; no borrowings at balance date so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- risk is charged once, in the flows and the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2026 cash lease payments 44.3 (principal 36.2 in financing + lease interest 8.1) = 1.9% of sales, deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (42.0 current + 170.7 non-current = 212.7) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (106.0 - 36.6 = 69.4, 3.0% of sales) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, IFRS-16 treatment B). Cochlear is a debt-free operating medtech company; routing table row 'operating company, non-US'. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). BASE REVENUE is FY26 'sales revenue' 2,343.4 (the company's primary measure, excludes FX-contract gains; statutory revenue 2,347.6) because the margin paths are built on it. EBITDA MARGIN PATH is underlying EBITDA (underlying EBIT + total D&A, post-IFRS-16) on sales revenue, NET of an assumed residual cloud-programme expense: FY26 underlying EBIT 432.6 + D&A 106.0 = 538.6 (23.0%) before the 94.3 pre-tax cloud computing expense the company classifies as a significant item (FY25 32.7). That cloud spend is real cash and the programme had not been declared complete, so the base charges a further 1.5% of sales in FY27 and 0.5% in FY28 -- a judgment, not a disclosed number. FY26 underlying also absorbed 69 of transitional costs (32 restructuring, 37 STI replenishment). FY27 GUIDANCE (FY26 AR Chair/CEO outlook): low single-digit constant-currency sales growth, underlying NPAT 330-350 (midpoint +5.5% on 322.4); year-1 base margin is backed out of the midpoint (EBIT ~457 at a 25% tax rate = ~18.9% + 4.5% D&A). FY26 guidance was cut twice (435-460 in Aug-25, 'lower end' at H1, revised again in April). REPORTED_FCF 241.1 = operating cash flow 368.0 - capex 90.7 - lease principal 36.2 (CSV FreeCashFlow of 277.3 is before lease principal; the company's own 'free cash flow' of 263.5 also deducts 13.8 other investments). LAST_FCF 204.3 = 241.1 - 26.6 - 10.2. FY26 FCF is not a clean base: it carries the 94.3 cloud cash cost and a 58.6 working-capital release after the FY25 Nexa inventory build -- which is why the forward flows are built from components. INTEREST INCOME 10.2 stripped (net cash 187.7 is in the bridge) although net cash is below 1x FCF. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables + inventory - payables = 789.1, 34% of sales, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture_pct is negative. CAPEX 4.0% of sales vs 90.7 (3.9%) FY26 'stay-in-business' capex. TAX: underlying effective rate 25% (R&D incentives, offshore mix) vs cash tax paid 131.9; 26% used throughout. BUYBACK: on-market buyback inactive in FY26 (0.1; FY25 28.3, FY24 43.0); the flat count is funded by the 26.6 award outlay. Dividends 281.2 paid FY26; final dividend cut 40% to $1.30 (FY26 total $3.45, 70% payout of underlying NPAT). Scenario axes are drawn from the FY2026 annual report's review of operations and cross-checked against COH.AX_Analysis.json (referral-pathway inconsistency, margin fragility, FX, China VBP, guidance credibility).

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Bottom of FY27 guidance with 2.0% cloud expense recurring for two years; margin never recovers past ~18.5% underlying EBIT (the FY26 level) as low-tier emerging-market mix and under-recovered manufacturing overhead persist.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Year 1 = FY27 guidance midpoint (23.4%) less 1.5% assumed residual cloud expense; year 2 = 24.3% less 0.5%. Matures at 26.5% = ~22% underlying EBIT margin, the FY24 level (22.4%) and below FY25 (23.5% ex cloud); implies ~16% net margin against the company's long-standing 18% aspiration.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Top of FY27 guidance, cloud programme ends after a 1.0% FY27 charge; matures at ~24% underlying EBIT margin = the 18% net margin target.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): guidance was cut twice in FY26, the developed-market slowdown is across several countries at once and China VBP is a structural price reset; but there is no balance-sheet or solvency risk and the installed base makes services revenue sticky. Base 50%: FY27 guidance already assumes only a modest recovery. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs developed-market volume re-acceleration AND gross-margin recovery AND the cloud spend ending, which are related but not guaranteed to arrive together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
